State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Sanjay Ambadas Joshi vs Colonel P.K.Sharma on 8 July, 2013
1

MAHARASHTRA STATE CONSUMER DISPUTE REDRESSAL
COMMISSION,MUMBAI, CIRCUIT BENCH AT AURANGABAD.

 Date of filing :25/04/2007
 Date of order :08/07/2013

1. FIRST APPEAL NO. : 364 OF 2007
 IN COMPLAINT CASE NO.: 32/2004
 DISTRICT CONSUMER FORUM :AURANGABAD.

Sanjay Ambadas Joshi
M.D.Tushman Construction Pvt. Ltd
R/o.Amaya Sahajeevan Colony,
Samarth nagar,Aurangabad. Appellant.

 VERSUS.

Colonel P.K.Sharma
R/o.Plot No. 6 K.D.R.Firms,
Sharnapur Tq & Dist.
Aurangabad. Respondent

2. F.A.No.376 OF 2007 IN CC NO.: 32/2004

Colonel P.K.Sharma
R/o.Plot No. 6 K.D.R.Firms,
Sharnapur Tq & Dist.
Aurangabad. Appellant

VERSUS.

Sanjay Ambadas Joshi
M.D.Tushman Construction Pvt. Ltd
R/o.Amaya Sahajeevan Colony,
Samarth nagar,Aurangabad. Respondent.

CORAM : Mr.S.M.Shembole, Hon`ble Presiding Judicial Member.
Mr.K.B.Gawali, Hon`ble Member.
Mrs.Uma Bora, Hon'ble Member.
Present : Adv.Shri.G.M.Kubade is present for the appellant.
Shri.B.B.Kulkarni is present for the respondent builder.
O R A L O R D E R
2
Per Mr.K.B.Gawali, Hon`ble Member.
1. These are the cross appeals which have been directed against
the same judgment and order dated 31/01/2007 passed by the Dist.
Forum, Aurangabad in C.C.No. 32/2004, thereby allowing the
complaint partly. The appeal No. 364/2007 is filed by the original
opponent namely Shri. Sanjay Joshi who is the builder/developer
seeking quashing of the impugned judgment and order whereas the
appeal No. 376/2007 is filed by the original complainant namely
Colonel Shri.P.K.Sharma seeking additional relief as per the
complaint. For better understanding the appellant in appeal No.
364/2007 herein after is termed as " opponent/developer" whereas
the appellant in appeal No. 376/2007 is termed as the "Complainant"
2. Since the issue involved in both these appeals are same and
hence we have decided to disposed off these appeals by a common
judgment and order.
3 (a) The brief facts leading to the present appeals are as under.
That, the opponent developer Shri.Sanjay Joshi had floated a
Residential Farm House Scheme namely "Krishna Devrai Farm"
consisting of 67 houses, in G.No. 79 of village Sharanapur Tq. & Dist.
Aurangabad covering the area of 6.94 H. abutting on Aurangabad-
Nashik-Mumbai highway road at about 11 k.m. away from
Aurangabad city. That the opponent developer had given publicity to
the said scheme by way of brochure in which he had assured to
provide the facilities such as Wide roads with Sodium Vapor Lamps,
Individual Telephones, Club House, Swimming Pool, Tennis Court,
Restaurant, Gymnasium,Health Club, Department Store, Dispensary,
and many more as specified therein. That, the complainant is an ex-
army Colonel and was posted in Cantonment in Aurangabad in June
2001. That, he was to retire from service in the month of Sept. 2002
and therefore had planed to settle at Aurangabad. That the developer
3
had come in to his contact and by giving information about the said
scheme had given him offer to purchase the farm house. Accordingly,
the complainant accepted the offer and booked the farm house with
plot bearing No. 6 admeasuring area of 7457 sq. feet including built
up area of 1100 sq. feet for consideration of Rs 8.00 lakhs on the
condition that he should be given possession of the said house before
Diwali 2002.
3(b) That, accordingly the complainant paid to the
opponent/developer Rs 8.00 lakhs towards the cost of the house & Rs
3.85 lakhs towards excess work as per demand. Thus, he paid total
amount of Rs 11.85 lakhs in five instalments up to Dec. 2002 but the
opponent/developer failed to give the possession up to Oct. 2002 as
orally agreed by him. That, even the agreement to sale was executed
on 29/01/2003 after heavy persuation. The sale deed was executed
on 01/10/2003 and possession of the said house was given on the
same date of sale deed i.e. after the delay of 10 months.
3© After having received the possession the complainant raised
various grievances against the developer such as charging excess
amount of Rs 3.85 lakhs towards cost of the house etc. and non
existance of facilities as assured in brochure and agreement of sale.
That, there was no safe drinking water facility, no electric supply
although Rs 20,000/- was paid for the same. No road with Sodium
Vapur lamp. No septic tank, no wide road, no security wall and so on.
That, the quality of the construction was also poor as within three
months of possession there were various cracks in the walls and
leakages in the roof. The complainant had also issued legal notice
dated 22/10/2003 to the developer to comply with the above said
lacunas and deficiencies but since there was no response from the
developer, he filed the present complaint seeking direction to the
developer to provide the said facilities as promised in the agreement
and also sought direction to pay:
1. Excess amount of Rs 3.85 lakhs.
4
2. Interest on the amount of Rs 11.85 lakhs @ 5 % from Dec.
2002 to 2003.
3. Interest on Rs 3.85 lakhs from Oct. 2003 up to the date of
 judgment @ 18 %
4. Rs 85000/- towards the rent paid during the period from Dec.
2002 to Oct. 2003.
5. Rs 47,066/- towards the digging expenses of bore well.
6. Rs 50,000/- for difference in rates of extra work.
7. Rs 670/- for water testing bill.
8. Rs 3202/- for the repairs of electronic appliances. i.e. total
amount of Rs 6.20 lakhs in addition, he also sought direction for the
compensation of Rs 2 lakhs for the mental harassment and cost of the
complaint.
4(a) The, opponent developer appeared before the Forum and
resisted the claim of the complainant. It was contended by him that as
per the "Agreement to Sale" the possession was to be given within ten
(10) months from the date of execution of the sale of agreement i.e.
29/01/2003. Therefore possession was supposed tobe given on or
before 29/11/2003 but the actual possession was given on
01/10/2003 i.e. about 2 months in advance. Hence, the
complainant's claim for rent was baseless. It was further submitted
that the actual cost of the said house was fixed at Rs 11.85 lakhs and
not Rs 8 lakhs. That just to avoid to pay the stamp duty and other
charges the complainant had insisted to show the cost of Rs 8 lakhs
only. Hence, he contended that the complainant was not entitled to
receive Rs 3.85 lakh. He further submitted that the amount of Rs
1,59,800/- was paid to him towards extra work done on the request
of the complainant and hence he was not entitled to get the refund of
Rs 50,000/-.
4(b) The opponent/developer further submitted that the amenities
i.e. safe drinking water, electric supply, play ground, space for
greenery were provided on site. However, the work of other amenities
5
such as septic tank, roads, security wall and street light were in
progress. As regards other public amenities they were not viable to be
provided as there were only four families had occupied their
houses. That, as for as the quality of construction is concerned, the
complainant had made false and distorted allegations. He had also
contended that no electric charges of Rs 20,000/- were paid by the
complainant. He further submitted that as the safe drinking water
supply was made available to the complainant he was not entitled to
get the amount of Rs 47,066/- as the claim towards digging expenses
of bore well. He also submitted that as the water testing report was
issued by the government authority there was no need for the
complainant to get the water tested on his own. That as per the water
testing report the water was clean and potable. He therefore denied
the claim of Rs 670/- also as made by the complainant. The claim of
complainant of Rs 3202/- for the repairs of electronic appliances has
also been denied on the ground that required electric supply was
made available to the complainant and hence he was not responsible
for any alleged damages to the electric appliances. He thus contended
that the complaint being false and frivolous be dismissed with cost of
Rs 10,000/-.
5(a) The Dist. Forum during the hearing of the complaint had
appointed Ld. Counsel Shri. S.T.Agrawal as a "Court Commissioner"
who submited his spot inspection report on 28/07/2004. The Dist.
Forum Aurangabad after perusal of the paper, the said spot inspection
report of the Court Commission and after hearing of the parties by
way of its judgment and order dated 27/07/2005 had allowed the
complaint partly and directed the opponent/developer to complete the
work of club house, dispensary, tennis court, swimming pool etc.
within a period of one year and to repair of the cracks of the house. As
regards the claim of the complainant about refund of excess payment
of Rs 3.85/- lakhs, rental amount of refund of Rs 50,000/- alleged to
have taken against extra work it was held by the Dist. Forum that the
6
grievance relating to it were being about the pricing of the property,
was beyond jurisdiction of the Dist. Forum and therefore it had
directed the complainant to approach to the Civil Court.
5(b) Aggrieved by the said judgment and order both the complainant
and opponent/developer filed the cross appeals bearing Nos. 1529/05
and 1514/05 before this Commission at Mumbai. The State
Commission Mumbai after hearing these appeals had set aside the
impugned judgment and order of the Dist. Forum and remanded the
complaint back for fresh enquiry and decision holding that the Forum
was competent to decide as to whether the excess price was recovered
by the opponent/developer from the complainant purchaser and to
grant appropriate relief.
5©. Accordingly the Dist. Forum after having given fresh hearing to
both the sides and after perusal of the record has passed the
impugned and order dated 31/01/2007 against which present cross
appeals have been filed. By way of it's said judgment and order the
Dist. Forum partly allowed the complaint and directed the
opponent/developer to pay to the complainant Rs 3.85 lacks which
was held to have been recovered in excess of the price of the house
with interest @ 9 % p.a. within six weeks. It was further directed to
repair the cracks of the walls and to pay Rs 20,000/- towards mental
harassment along with Rs 2000/- as cost of the complaint. The other
claims of the complainant have been held by the Dist. Forum as not
proved and hence, no relief was given.
6(a) Feeling dissatisfied and discontented, the present cross appeals
have been filed which came to be finally heard on 08/04/2013 and
were reserved for judgment and order. However, before passing of the
judgment and order the Judicial Member was changed and hence
both the appeals were reheard on 20/06/2013. Adv.Shri.
B.B.Kulkarni was present for the appellant whereas Adv.
7
Shri.G.M.Kubade was present for the complainant. Both these counsel
have submitted their written notes of arguments and also made detail
oral submissions.
6(b) The Ld. Counsel Shri. Kubade for the complainant submitted
that the opponent/developer had admitted in his written reply about
the price of the said farm house as Rs 8 lakh though he received Rs
11.85 lakh and also further received Rs 1,59,800/- for additional
construction. He further submitted that even as per the sale deed the
price of the farm house has been shown as Rs 8 lakhs. He therefore
contended that the developer was liable to refund Rs 3.85 lakhs with
interest as recovered in excess of the price. He also contended that the
value of the extra work was assessed by the complainant through his
Architest Shri. Nitin Bagdiya on 31/03/2004 from which it was
revealed that the developers had charged excess amount of Rs
50,000/- towards extra work done. He therefore contended that
complainant was entitled to receive the said extra amount of Rs
50,000/-. He also averred that as per oral agreement the developer
had agreed to hand over the possession of the farm house in Oct.
2002 after receipt of the amount of construction cost of the house i.e.
Rs 8 lakhs. However, actual possession was given on 01/10/2003 i.e.
almost after the delay of one year. He further submitted that the
complainant paid last instalment of Rs 1.35 lakh on 31/12/2002 i.e.
total being of Rs 11.85 lakh and then only the agreement to sale was
executed by the builder. Hence, he contended that the developer was
liable to pay interest on the amount of Rs 11.85 lakhs @ 9 % p.a. for
one year. On the same ground of delay in delivery of possession, he
claimed rent of the house of Rs 85,000/- for the period of 10 months.
His further contention was that the developer did not supply the
potable drinking water to the complainant's farm house which was
evident from the Court Commission Shri.S.T.Agrawal's report and
hence he had to spent Rs 47,066/- towards taking up of the bore well.
The developers was responsible to pay Rs 670/- which the
8
complainant had paid towards charges of water testing. He further
claimed Rs 3202/- towards damages to the electronic appliance,
caused due to non-supply of regular electric supply.
The Ld. Copunsel Shri.Kubade further submitted that the
contention of the developer that he was not bound to provide the
facilities as mentioned in the brochure was not acceptable. He
contended that it was on the basis of the offer of various facilities as
promised in the said brochure the complainant along with other
purchasers had booked the farm house and hence it was binding on
him to provide all those facilities. He further contended that even the
facilities as per the agreement to sale have not been provided by the
developer. He therefore averred that the developer had failed to
provide all the basic amenities and also other facilities as agreed upon
and hence, the developer was rightly charged by the complainant as to
have committed deficiency is service and had also indulged in to
unfair trade practice. He also contended that the Dist. Forum has
granted a megre amount of compensation of Rs 20,000/- towards
mental agony and physical harassment, as the complainant had been
fighting for justice against the developer since long. He therefore
alleged that the Dist. Forum has failed to appreciate the evidence on
record and only partly allowed the complaint and requested to modify
the impugned judgment and order suitably so as to grant entire relief
to the complainant as per his complaint.
In support of his above said contention he relied on the
following case laws.
1. Ghaziabad Development Authority - V/s- Union of India and
another (2000) 6 Supreme Court Cases 113. In which it is held by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court that the brochure issued by the development
authority amounts to an offer which having been accepted results in
the contract between applicant and the authority. Hence, in case of
9
breach of contract the damages may be claimed by one party against
the other parties.
2. Bareilly Development Authority - V/s- Vrinda Gujarati and
others (2004) 4 Supreme Court Cases 606 . In which it is held by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court that the allotters having entered into the
realm of contract with authority would be bound by the terms thereof
and it was obligatory on the part of Dev.Authority to provide the flats
on contractual price.
3. Haryana Urban Development Authority - V/s V.P.Mutreja
(2004) 13 Supreme Court Cases 692 in which it is held by the Hon'ble
Supreme Court that there is delay in delivery of the possession and
therefore the allottee is entitled to the relief of interest on the amount
paid by him.
4. Haryana Urban Development Authority -V/s- Shital Parshad
Jain (2005) 9 supreme Court Cases 438. It is observed by the Hon'ble
Supreme Court, that in cases like the present one where monies are
directed to be refunded the interest should be as per the
Interest Act
.
5. Pushpa Builders Flat Buyers Association - V/s- Pushpa
Builders Ltd and others 616 by National Commission.
6. The Chandrasekharpur Housing Board Colony Unnayan Samiti
- V/s- The State of Orissa & Ors. CPR 1-1992 by State Consumer
Disputes Redressal Commission, Orissa, Cuttak. In which it is
observed by the State Commission that the promises held out in the
brochure requires to be fulfilled by the development authority.
6© On the other hand Ld. counsel Shri.B.B.Kulkarni for the
opponent/developer submitted that the claim of the complainant were
false and frivolous. He specifically denied the contention of the
complainant that the cost of the said farm house was fixed for Rs 8
lakh and submitted that the cost was fixed at Rs 11.85 lakhs. In
support of his contention the Ld. counsel Shri. Kulkarni referred to
the F.I.R. lodged by the complainant against the developer in which
the complainant has made a statement that he had a oral agreement
10
with developer in the of Nov. 2002 as per which the cost of the farm
house was decided at Rs 11.85 lakh. The Ld. counsel further contened
that only to reduce the burden of stamp duty the complainant had
insisted to show the cost of the house at Rs 8 lakh in the sale deed
and therefore the complainant was not entitled to receive the alleged
refund of Rs 3.85 lakhs. As regards claim of interest on Rs 3.85 lakh
and the claim of rental amount of Rs 85,000/- for alleged delay of 10
months caused in giving possession he had also stated the said
claims as baseless. He further submitted that the developer had
never agreed to deliver the possession in the month of Oct. 2002. On
the other hand he stated that as per "agreement to sale" the
possession was to be given within 10 months from the date of
execution of said agreement i.e on or before 29/11/2003. However,
the same was given in the months of Oct. 2003 i.e. about two month
in advance.
The Ld. counsel Shri. Kulkarni further contended that the
developer had supplied all the facilities to the complainant as specified
in the agreement such as drinking water, road, sanitation, electricity,
space for greenery and play ground which was supported by the
Court Commissioner Adv.Shri.S.T.Agrawal's report and hence the
developer was not liable to pay the claim towards the cost of digging
of bore well as claimed at Rs 47066/-. He also denied the charges of
Rs 670/- towards testing of water etc. As for as the claim about cost
of Rs 3202/- towards damages of electronic compliances he submitted
that the complainant had failed to prove the damages to the electric
appliances and hence said claim was not acceptable. As regards other
common facilities such as club house, swimming pool, dispensary and
tennis court etc could not be put in function as only four families had
occupied their houses. He therefore, contended that the Dist. Forum
had failed to properly appreciated the evidence as produced by the
developer and has wrongly passed the impugned judgement and
order which required tobe set aside.
11
In support of his above said submission he relied upon
following citations:
1. Shri.S.Srinivasa Murthy - V/s- Karnataka Housing Board 2012
(4) CPR 4 (SC) in which case the respondent Housing Board with the
consent of the appellant had shown 81 % of the total cost in the
registration deed. Therefore, it is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court
that the appellant /complainant is estopped from claiming refund.
2. Hoshiarpur Improvement Trush - V/s- Major Amrit Lal Saini
2008 (1) CPR 202 (NC) in which it is held by Hon'ble National
Commission that the Consumer Forum can not go in to the question
of pricing as the price is already fixed by the said statutory body i.e.
appellant.
7. We have perused the papers including case laws referred by the
revial parties and also gave our anxious thought to the arguments
advanced by the Ld. counsel of both the parties. The important points
which come up for our consideration and decision are :
01. Whether the complainant is entitled to the claims made by him
in his complaint?.
02. Whether the judgment and order passed by the Dist. Forum is
just and proper.
As regards the first points we have to verify the claim wise
entitlement of the complainant. There are two types of claim.
A) Non-Monetary and (B) Monetary
A) Non-Monetary Claim i.e. seeking direction to the developer to
provide all facilities as promised in the agreement.
I) On perusal of the agreement to sale it is seen that the developer
has promised following facilities to be provided and hence the
complainant is entitled to receive the same.
12
i. Compound wall to the farm house and to the entire colony.
ii. Common colony access.
iii. Common open space for play ground.
iv. Necessary arrangement of sanitation.
v. Space for greenery.
vi. Necessary arrangement of drinking water.
vii. Common amenities centre.
Now the question is whether these facilities have been provided
by the developer to the complainant at the time of taking possession of
the farm house. To verify this aspect we referred to the report dated
28/07/2004 of the Court Commissioner Shri.Agrawal who was
appointed at the instance of the present complainant. Perusal of this
report reveals that there were hair crakes to the plaster of walls in
three rooms and wall crack in dressing room. The status regarding
the facilities was as under :
i. Compound wall to the farm house was completed however the
 Common compound wall to the colony was incomplete.
ii. Independent electric connection through D.P. was given.
iii. Water pipe connection was found given only up to the gate and
 not to the farm house of the complainant although common
 water supply facility from well was found available.
iv. Construction of common septic tank was in progress.
v. Common colony road of WBM wAS provided but no Sodium
 Vapour Lamps.
vi. Open space of about 30,000 sq.ft. was also made available.
II) It is thus apparent that as specified in the agreement the
developer had not provided the drinking water facility and the
sanitation arrangement including common septic tank etc. which
was in progress. Thus to the extent of these basic amenities the
developer can be charged to have committed deficiency in service.
13
III) As regards common amenity centre as promised in the
agreement and other facilities as agreed in broacher i.e. Swimming
Pool, health club, dispensary etc. were not provided as per the report
of the Court Commissioner. However, as Per.Sec. 12 (1) © of the
Consumer Protection Act
, individual complainant can not seek the
relief in the matter of common interest without the permission of the
Dist. Forum. In the present case the complainant has filed the
complaint in his individual capacity and hence, we are of the view that
he is not entitled to get any direction regarding providing of all these
common facilities.
B Monetary Claims
I) Refund of excess amount of Rs 3.85 lakh along with interest
@ 18 % :
It is the contention of the complainant that as per the sale
deed , the price of the house is shown as Rs 8 lakh against which he
has paid total amount of Rs 1185 lakhs hence he is claiming the
refund of Rs 385 lakhs. The question is when the consideration of the
said house was fixed Rs 8 lakhs why did he pay Rs 11.85 lakhs. It is
also worth to be noted that he had made police complaint against the
developer in which case FIR bearing No. 132/2006 was registered. In
his statement recorded in that FIR, the complainant has admitted that
as per oral agreement the price of the farm house was fixed at Rs
11.85 lakhs. There is also contrary statement made by the
complainant in his complaint stating that he had paid Rs 8 lakhs
towards consideration of the house and Rs 3.85 towards cost of extra
work. Therefore, considering all these facts the contention of the
complainant that the cost of the house was fixed at Rs 8 lakhs is not
sustainable and can not be accepted. The Dist. Forum has however
failed to appreciate the above said evidence on record and wrongly
accepted the claim by way of its impugned judgment and order.
14
II). Interest on amount of Rs 11.85 lakh @ 5 % p.a. from Dec.
2002 to Sept. 2003 and Rs 85,000/- towards the rent paid during
this period due to delay in giving possession :
It is contended by the complainant that as per oral agreement
the possession of the Farm house was to be delivered in the month of
Oct. 2002 ( Diwali Festival of 2002 ). However, the possession was
delivered in Oct. 2003 i.e. almost after the delay of one year. He has
therefore claimed the interest on the amount of Rs 11.85 paid to the
developer and rent for the period from Jan. 2003 as the final
instalment of Rs 1.35 lakh was paid on 31/12/2002. This claim is
denied by the developer stating that no such oral agreement had
taken place and further contended that as per the agreement to sale
dated 29/01/2003 the possession was to be given within 10 months
i.e by 29/11/2003 but the same was delivered on 01/10/2013 i.e.
almost 2 months in advance. It is interesting to note that in order to
establish that the total consideration of the house was fixed Rs 11.85
lakhs the complainant has relied on the statement of the
complainant in the police case in which he had admitted that there
was a oral agreement. The developer therefore can not deny that there
was no oral agreement. It is also to be noted that prior to the
execution of the "Agreement to Sale" the complainant had paid the
entire amount of consideration by the end of Dec. 2002. We also get
support to believe the contention of the complainant about the oral
agreement by the developer to deliver possession in Oct. 2002 as he
was to retire from service in Sept. 2002 and was required to vacate
the Government accommodation. It is also to be noted that during the
said period of 10 months the developer himself has provided
accommodation to the complainant on rent but stated to have not
received the amount of rent. We thus find that there was a delay in
giving possession and hence this claim of the complainant is
acceptable. However, the Dist. Forum has failed to consider the said
claim.
15
III) Rs 47066/- towards the begging expenses of bore well :
It is apparent from the Court Commissioner Shri.S.T.Agrawal's
report dated 28/07/2004 that there was no piped drinking water
supply to the farm house of the complainant. In fact in such a
independent housing project it is the responsibility of the
builder/developer to provide basic amenities to each and individual
house. In the sale deed also it is mentioned that the arrangement of
water supply was being under taken which means that on the date of
possession there was no arrangement of drinking water and even
after 9 months of taking possession i.e. on the date of spot inspection
as per the report of Shri.Agrsawal the water connection was given
only up to the gate of the complainant's house. Hence, as there was
no drinking water supply to the complainant, he was forced to make
an alternate arrangement of water supply by way of bore well and
hence his claim for the payment of the same stands acceptable.
IV) Rs 50,000/- for different of rates of extra work :
Undisputedly, the complainant has paid the amount of Rs
1,59,000/- towards extra work done by the developer at his instance.
It is after making payment and almost after five months of taking
possession the complainant has got the valuation done of this extra
work at Rs 1,09,000/-on 31/03/2004 through his Architest on the
basis of which he claimed the difference amount of Rs 50,000/-. In
fact this valuation can not be accepted as the same is done by the
complainant through his private Architect and that too after the
period of about 5 months of taking possession. Secondly the
complainant has also not produced on record the comparative
statement of item wise expenditure to prove the excess amount
recovered by the developer. Hence, this claim is not sustainable and
the Dist. Forum has rightly rejected the same.
V) Rs 670/- towards water testing bill and Rs 3202/- for the
repairs of the electronic appliances :
16
Both these claims are not acceptable as they have not been
proved against the developer. It is observed from the record that the
developer had got the water tested from the Government authority the
result of which was said to be as potable water. The question is
therefore why the complainant was required to test the water.
Further, as observed by the Dist. Forum the complainant has not
given details as to which of the water he had got tested.
As regards the repairs charges of the electronic appliances there
is no proof to show that there was alleged damages. In fact as per the
Court Commissioners report the complainant was provided with
independent electronic connection through the D.P. Hence, if at all
there was any alleged damage, the developer can not be held
responsible for the same.
VI) Rs 2 lakh towards compensation of the mental and physical
harassment:
True it is that the developer has failed to provide proper service
to the extent of certain defects in the construction i.e. crack of the
walls, non-supply of basic amenities such as drinking water, delay in
handing over the possession etc. The complainant therefore is
entitled to get compensation for which he is fighting since about last
10 years . The Dist. Forum vide its impugned judgment and order has
directed to repair the cracks to the wall. But as the period of about 10
years has been lapsed this direction of repairing the said defects does
not appears to be proper and practicable and hence we are of the view
to consider the same deficiency while granting compensation. The
Dist. Forum has awarded compensation Rs 20,000/- towards mental
and physical harassment which appears tobe quite insufficient.
Considering the various deficiencies committed by the developer in
providing proper service to the complainant we are of the view to grant
lumpsum compensation Rs 75,000/- towards mental/physical
harassment including the cost of repairs.
17
8. In view of the aforesaid facts and observations. We are inclined
to partly allow both the appeals by modifying the impugned judgment
and order. In the result we pass the following order.
O R D E R
1. Both the appeals bearing No. 364/2007 and 376/2007 are
partly allowed.
2. The impugned judgment and order passed by the Dist. Forum is
hereby modified as under.
i. The opponent/developer is directed to pay to the complainant
Rs 85,000/- towards rental amount and also interest @ 5 % p.a. on
the amount of Rs 11.85 lakh for the period from 01/01/2003 to
01/10/2003 as claimed by the complainant for the delay caused in
giving possession of the house.
ii. The opponent/developer is further directed to pay to the
complainant Rs 47,066/- towards expenses incurred for digging bore
well with interest @ 6 % p.a. from the date of filing of complaint till its
realisation.
iii. The opponent/developer is further directed to pay to the
complainant the lump sum compensation of Rs 75,000/- towards
mental and physical harassment including the cost of repairs.
iv. The opponent/developer is also directed to pay Rs 5,000/-
towards cost of the proceedings and bear his own cost.
v. All the above said amounts are directed to be paid within a
